title: Overweight French Bulldog: Risks, Body Condition and Weight Loss
description: How to tell if you have an overweight French Bulldog, how extra weight worsens BOAS and spine problems, and how to plan safe weight loss with your vet.
secondaryKeywords: how much should a french bulldog weigh

faq.q: How much should a French Bulldog weigh?
faq.a: The AKC standard sets a maximum of 28 lb, and the FCI range is about 20 to 31 lb for males and 18 to 29 lb for females. Body condition matters more than the number: you should feel the ribs easily and see a waist.

faq.q: How do I know if my French Bulldog is overweight?
faq.a: If you have to press to feel the ribs, there is no waist from above, or the belly hangs instead of tucking up, your dog is likely above the ideal body condition of 4 to 5 out of 9. Ask your vet to score it.

faq.q: Does weight affect a French Bulldog's breathing?
faq.a: Yes. Studies link obesity and a thicker neck to higher BOAS risk, and excess weight to more breathing obstruction during sleep. Cambridge's BOAS grading includes weight loss as part of managing moderate BOAS.

faq.q: How can I help my French Bulldog lose weight safely?
faq.a: Work with your vet on a calorie target based on ideal weight, use a weight-loss diet rather than just cutting regular food, weigh portions, keep treats under 10% of calories and add gentle, cool walks.

faq.q: Can a French Bulldog puppy be overweight?
faq.a: Yes. Puppies should look sturdy, not round, and growing dogs need more frequent body condition checks. Measure food and ask your vet to score your puppy at each visit.
